observed_contract: Notion run_many() awaits every admitted child with return_exceptions=true, so a peer failure no longer cancels a sibling that may already be mutating local state.
After all children settle, run_many() raises the first BaseException and discards successful sibling DelegationResult objects.
The finally block releases every reserved task_id, including siblings that completed successfully.
The existing peer-failure test proves the successful sibling finishes but intentionally expects only the exception; it does not preserve/replay that successful result on a batch retry.
Qwen runAgentSubagents(), by contrast, returns per-task structured results and persisted done tasks are resumed instead of executed again.
risk: If a caller retries the same Notion batch after one child fails, a sibling that already completed a write/shell action can run again because its successful result was discarded and its identity released. This is a same-process duplicate-side-effect path even before the separate process-restart durable-child-state gap.
minimal_product_contract: A partial batch outcome must be first-class: successful siblings cannot disappear merely because another sibling failed.
A retry of the same canonical child identity must replay a previously completed result rather than dispatch the child again.
Only failed siblings are eligible for ordinary retry; uncertain siblings remain blocked under the existing uncertainty contract.
For process-restart safety, the completed/failed/uncertain child ledger must eventually be durable; an in-memory cache only closes the immediate same-process duplicate path.
Do not solve this by cancelling successful siblings or by treating all partial failures as uncertain: that would lose useful completed work and reduce safe parallelism.
candidate_regression: Run batch [ok, fails] where ok performs one counted local side effect and returns successfully while fails raises.
Retry the identical batch in the same lifecycle.
Assert ok executor count remains 1 and its prior result is replayed; fails executor count becomes 2.
Extend the same assertion across restart once the durable child-state owner lands its storage contract.
